analysis.title: Factor Views 4Q 2026: Themes from the Quantitative Solutions team
key_insights: Factors posted a positive Q3 2026 on average, despite a sharp reversal in equity markets and unexpected geopolitical and monetary policy developments.
Equity value and equity quality performed well globally in Q3 and offset weakness in equity momentum.

Equity momentum had a sharp drawdown after one of its strongest multi-year runs and strong performance in 1H 2026. In July it had its worst month ever in the data set in emerging markets, developed Asia ex-Japan and Europe, and its second worst quarter globally.

Momentum recovered toward quarter end and dispersion normalized. Historically dispersion often tightens well past normal, which would reduce opportunities for the factor. The team recommends reducing momentum overweights without abandoning the factor, since it still diversifies against value and quality.

Equity value rebounded in Q3 after a weak Q2 with positive returns in all major regions. Emerging markets had their second strongest quarter in 30 years and developed Asia Pacific ex-Japan had its fourth best.

The global value factor is nearly one standard deviation inexpensive versus its long-term history on a sector-neutral basis, and more than one standard deviation inexpensive in the U.S. The team notes AI-driven uncertainty about future profitability makes it unclear whether some cheap companies are attractive or face structural disruption.

Equity quality had a strong Q3 after a difficult stretch, positive in all major markets except Europe and the UK, where it was modestly negative. Its recovery was the inverse of the momentum unwind as fundamentals returned as a driver of stock returns after July's reversal.

Quality is now more than one standard deviation inexpensive globally and more inexpensive in the U.S. This is despite U.S. consumer confidence at multi-decade lows. Historically low confidence correlated with higher valuations for high quality stocks, but that relationship has recently broken down.

Fundamental dispersion (such as ROE) between high and low quality businesses is attractive globally. With attractive starting valuations and renewed investor focus on fundamentals, the team keeps a positive longer-term view on quality.
Macro factors had an exceptional Q3, driven mainly by fixed income positioning and helped by equity and currency markets. Trend factors were above average, led by fixed income.

Short positioning across developed bond markets profited from rising yields. The rise was driven more by real yields than inflation expectations, as markets priced more hawkish central bank policy and higher bond issuance.

Equity trend factors were negative in Q3, hurt by long positions in rate-sensitive indexes (S&P 400, S&P 600) and by stock-level momentum reversals (Nasdaq 100, MSCI Emerging Markets). Commodity trend lost in 11 of 17 markets, mostly agriculturals (corn, live cattle, feeder cattle, sugar, wheat).
Macro alpha factors had their best quarter in the data set (dating to the early 2000s), led by government bond alpha. Equity index and currency alpha also rose. Commodities were weak.

Government bond relative value gained from shorts in German Bunds and U.S. Treasuries, offsetting losses from longs in UK Gilts and JGBs early in Q3. FX relative value gained from carry and valuation signals, with shorts in Swiss francs and longs in Japanese yen.

Trend signals moved much shorter in duration, from -0.2 to -0.8 on a -1 to 1 scale, led by U.S. Treasuries and European bonds. Equity trend signal fell from +0.5 to +0.3, and commodity trend signal rose from neutral to +0.2.
The outlook for macro factors in aggregate is neutral. There is opportunity if a reflationary regime continues, but risk if markets shift to pricing growth concerns.

Overall the team stays positive on equity factors (value and quality attractive, momentum at elevated risk), rates most macro factors neutral, and favors diversification across factors. It believes the global expansion remains intact and supports a pro-risk posture.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Low confidence historically coincided with higher quality factor valuations, but quality has instead declined, so the relationship has broken down.

macro_indicators.reading: rising sharply in Q3, driven more by real yields than inflation expectations
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hawkish central bank policy and more bond issuance drove yields up, which benefited short bond positioning in trend and alpha factors.

macro_indicators.reading: -0.8 at quarter end, from -0.2 at start (scale -1 to 1)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Trend positioning is near extreme short duration, led by U.S. Treasuries and European bonds.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce equity momentum factor overweights without abandoning the factor
trade_ideas.rationale: Momentum is fragile after a strong run and dispersion may tighten further, but it still diversifies against value and quality.

trade_ideas.description: Favor equity value and equity quality factors, diversified across factors
trade_ideas.rationale: Both are historically inexpensive on sector-neutral valuation spreads, and quality has attractive fundamental dispersion.
trade_ideas.risk: AI-driven disruption may mean some cheap stocks are structurally impaired.

risk_factors: Equity momentum is fragile and could see further dispersion tightening.
AI-related disruption may make some inexpensive value stocks structurally impaired.
Macro factors are at risk if markets shift toward pricing growth concerns.
Potential market disruption and elevated factor volatility.
Equity quality has declined even as U.S. consumer confidence has fallen, contradicting its historical relationship.
vol_and_positioning: Equity momentum entered Q3 with elevated factor volatility, growing dispersion and crowded positioning.
Momentum dispersion has fallen but could tighten further, which would reduce the factor's opportunity set.
Trend signals are near extreme short duration in fixed income (-0.8 average).
The team expects elevated factor volatility and potential market disruption, and recommends diversification among and across factors.
geopolitical: Continuing geopolitical tensions during Q3 2026 supported a commodities rally.
Disrupted Russian and Ukrainian grain exports hurt agricultural trend positioning.
Reopening of the U.S. border to Mexican cattle hurt livestock trend positions.

tension_points.bull_case: Value and quality are more than one standard deviation inexpensive in the U.S. and about one globally, with attractive fundamental dispersion and renewed investor focus on fundamentals.
tension_points.bear_case: AI creates uncertainty about future profitability, so some cheap businesses may face structural disruption. Quality has also declined despite low consumer confidence, breaking its historical relationship.

tension_points.bull_case: A continued reflationary regime offers opportunity, with trend signals strongly short duration and record macro alpha performance.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro factors are at risk if markets shift toward pricing in concerns about economic growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A market shift toward pricing in growth concerns.
